groups.name: Support, not a user tool
groups.note: Repositories that support the tools above. There is nothing here to launch.

tools.name: Halyard
tools.summary: A product owner's assistant that works a backlog upward to leadership and downward to stories and tasks. It runs locally: a PowerShell launcher, one .NET library, and a browser UI on 127.0.0.1.
tools.tagline: Works a backlog upward to leadership and downward to stories and tasks.

tools.name: Halyard Ballast
tools.summary: The sandbox repository Halyard writes to: synthetic and copied work items, created, reviewed and deleted on purpose. There is no code and no UI here.
tools.tagline: The sandbox repository Halyard writes its test work items to.

tools.name: Lazarette
tools.summary: Your credentials, stowed and locked aboard your own workstation. A Windows PowerShell 5.1 engine serves a local browser app on 127.0.0.1; the browser is the product.
tools.tagline: Credentials stowed and locked on your own workstation.

tools.name: Gangplank
tools.summary: A browser-first workspace that gets people without Git training safely onto GitHub and GitLab projects, from Windows PowerShell 5.1 and a browser; no git.exe, Node or Python on the workstation.
tools.tagline: Gets people without Git training safely onto GitHub and GitLab.

tools.name: PacketRat
tools.summary: Outlook triage into a human-reviewed action queue, run from a local Windows PowerShell 5.1 service with a browser UI.
tools.tagline: Turns Outlook mail into a reviewed queue of actions.

tools.name: Shellback
tools.summary: Workforce capability intelligence: employee-attested skills, kept separate from claims, in a local-first browser app.
tools.tagline: Employee-attested skills, kept separate from claims.

tools.name: SnapShackle
tools.summary: A local-first Windows screenshot and annotation studio using native Windows capture, a built-in PowerShell HTTP host, and an offline browser UI.

tools.name: Bowerbird
tools.summary: Local-first file intelligence and screenshot renaming for Windows PowerShell 5.1 and your existing web browser.
tools.tagline: File intelligence and screenshot renaming, local-first.

tools.name: Eight Bells
tools.summary: Local-first watchstanding log intelligence: quality review, evidence-linked turnover and lessons learned (v2).
tools.tagline: Watchstanding log review, turnover and lessons learned.

tools.name: Capstan
tools.summary: An open-source, local-first screen recorder and video editor for Windows.

tools.name: Semaphore
tools.summary: Semaphore is an analyst workbench for building dashboards from plain-English briefs, CSV files and configured database sources, meant to replace Qlik on thin clients. It runs locally: a PowerShell launcher and a browser UI on 127.0.0.1. Engineering preview.
tools.tagline: Dashboard builder for a single analyst, built to replace Qlik.

tools.name: Fairlead
tools.summary: One local address for every model. Fairlead is the model router behind the Fleet tools: it speaks the OpenAI and Anthropic APIs on http://127.0.0.1:8776, sends each request to the right cloud or local model, and keeps answering from local models when the internet or a provider goes down.
tools.tagline: One local address for every model.

tools.name: Windlass
tools.summary: Run very large local GGUF models (70B and up) on an ordinary PC by streaming them one layer at a time, behind an OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.tagline: Runs 70B and larger models on an ordinary PC by streaming layers.
tools.runNote: API only, no browser UI: the OpenAI-compatible API answers on http://127.0.0.1:8777/v1 (or the next free port in 8777-8779). Stop it with Ctrl+C in the console or src\Stop-Windlass.ps1.

tools.name: TalkForge
tools.summary: Client-side neural text-to-speech (Piper, ONNX Runtime Web/WASM) with offline local assets.
tools.tagline: Offline neural text-to-speech in the browser.

tools.name: Data Noodler
tools.tagline: Flat-file analytics: CSV, Parquet, Arrow and SQLite.

tools.name: Phoenix LAI
tools.summary: Local Gemma models on your GPU behind an OpenAI-compatible API, plus a Chrome app-window client.
tools.tagline: Local GPU model server with an OpenAI-style API and a chat client.

tools.name: Bridge Warden
tools.summary: A governance and orchestration layer between onboard AI agents and the ship. No agent touches the ship directly: every request is checked, logged, and the big ones go to a human.
tools.tagline: Governance between onboard AI agents and the ship: every request checked and logged, the big ones go to a human.
tools.portNote: Port 8774 is provisional: PORTS.md lists it for Eight-Bells, and Bridge Warden walks 8774-8776 until it gets its own block.
